narrative.overview:
A quiet rendition of Systems Labanotation: the discipline of a dance score without its symbols. Pages are white score paper ruled in ink; titles are set in tall condensed caps like a score's title lettering; content sits in plain ruled rows on a twelve-column staff. The only drawn mark is the plumb line (a short bar, a vertical string and a kite-shaped bob), used as the wordmark's companion in header and footer.

Density is calm and editorial. Each section opens on a full-width ink rule with a display heading in the left seven columns and a lede bottom-aligned in the right five. Rows below are separated by light hairlines, never boxed. Colour is almost absent: ink, greys, and a single blue reserved for "now" (focus and caret). Motion is limited to state transitions.

The owner rejected the full notation (score diagram, patterned blocks, legend) as too busy. Keep the score's discipline; do not reintroduce its symbols.
keyCharacteristics: Ink on white paper, one functional blue.
Tall condensed uppercase display over a plain humanist sans for reading.
Twelve-column ruled rows; no cards as structure.
A dark ink closing band on every page except the contact page.

rules.name: The Playhead Rule
rules.body: Blue marks "now" (focus ring and caret) and does no other job. Never use it for links, buttons, fills, icons, or decoration.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: Ink rules open and close structure (section heads, page titles, header, form sub-heads); hairline rules separate rows within it. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Title Lettering Rule
rules.body: The condensed display face is always uppercase at 0.9 leading, and appears only in headings, row titles, step numerals and the mobile menu links. Never set body copy, buttons, or form labels in it.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: Tracked caps are margin notes, not headlines' introductions. They label the wordmark, footer columns, and definition terms; never put a small caps line above a heading.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Content is ruled rows on the twelve-column grid. Never group items into bordered, filled or shadowed cards.

rules.name: The Flat Score Rule
rules.body: No box-shadows, no lifted surfaces. If something needs separation, rule it or change its ground.

dos: Do open each section with a full-width ink rule, the headline in seven columns and the lede in five.
Do lay content out as hairline-separated rows on the twelve-column grid.
Do keep the condensed display face uppercase at 0.9 leading, and keep reading text in Public Sans.
Do close every page except contact with the ink band and its paper button.
Do pair one ink button with at most one line button in any action group.
donts: Don't use Playhead Blue for anything except focus and caret.
Don't build card grids, rounded corners, or shadows.
Don't add a second mark, logo device, or decorative notation (score diagrams, patterned blocks, legends).
Don't put tracked caps above headings as kickers or eyebrows; tracked caps belong to the wordmark, footer heads, and definition terms.
Don't set split heroes with a product image beside the headline, or rows of icon cards.
